lesson.child_mission: Aboriginal peoples and Torres Strait Islander peoples are two distinct groups, together called First Nations Peoples. There are many different Nations, each with its own languages, laws and ways of life, so no single description fits all. Their cultures are living and continuing.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Which is more accurate: "All Aboriginal people have the same culture" or "There are many First Nations with different languages and customs"? Which sources help?

FEEDBACK
The second. Sources such as the AIATSIS map, books by First Nations authors and local Aboriginal educators show the diversity.

WATCH FOR
Talking about First Nations Peoples only in the past tense, or as one group, hides that cultures continue and differ between Nations.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Make a respectful fact file on First Nations Peoples using two published sources. Include two ways Nations differ, one question to ask a local Aboriginal educator and the names of the sources. Do not guess about any Nation.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
